stories.title: Quest Alliance founder named to TIME100 Next India list
stories.summary: Aakash Sethi, founder of Quest Alliance, has been named to the inaugural TIME100 Next India 2026 list. His organization integrates AI readiness and self-learning into government schools and vocational institutes. The recognition highlights the persistent gap between classroom instruction and the specific skills required by modern workplaces.

stories.title: IMI revamps PGDM curriculum to emphasize AI fluency
stories.summary: The International Management Institute is shifting its Delhi, Kolkata and Bhubaneswar campuses toward career-focused MBA courses. CEO Suresh Ramanathan says the future manager must be AI-fluent and distinctly human. The school is currently redesigning its curriculum to ensure students remain relevant in an increasingly automated professional landscape.

stories.title: STEM interest fails to translate into engineering careers - report - The Engineer
Indian students prioritize UK job prospects over degree prestige
stories.summary: A LeapScholar report indicates Indian students increasingly select UK universities based on post-study employment potential rather than rankings. Interest in AI-related courses rose 43 percent this year. For many, a master's degree is now viewed primarily as a strategic investment to secure a work visa.

stories.title: Students urged to treat study abroad as a career pathway
stories.summary: International education is shifting from a focus on university admissions to long-term career planning. Experts suggest students evaluate employment prospects, practical experience and post-study pathways before selecting a destination. The decision is no longer just about the course, but the entire professional trajectory that follows graduation.

stories.title: Uniqlo invites students to leadership program in Tokyo
stories.summary: Fast Retailing is accepting applications for its 2027 Global Management Program in Tokyo. The six-day intensive event offers undergraduate and postgraduate students a chance to learn from business executives and industry experts. Participants will study the global fashion-retailing industry through a fully funded leadership and development curriculum.

stories.title: MTN Foundation awards 510 scholarships to Nigerian students
stories.summary: The MTN Foundation has awarded scholarships to 510 Nigerian students and inducted 358 graduates into its alumni community. The program supports high-performing students in science and technology, as well as those with visual impairments. The initiative aims to expand access to education and nurture young talent.

stories.title: I&M Foundation and Moringa School offer software scholarships
stories.summary: The I&M Foundation and Moringa School have launched a scholarship program providing fully funded software engineering training for young Kenyans. Beneficiaries receive full tuition coverage and a laptop. The partnership aims to expand access to technology education and create career development opportunities within the digital economy.

stories.title: KPMG Nigeria opens applications for university scholarships
stories.summary: KPMG Nigeria is accepting applications for its 2026 University Scholarship Programme. The initiative supports high-performing students at federal universities to enable access to education and lifelong learning. Applicants must be Nigerian citizens who have completed their secondary education. The deadline for submissions is December 10.

stories.title: St Agnes student enters Golden Book of World Records
stories.summary: Melora Risha Dsouza, a student at St Agnes School in Mangaluru, has entered the Golden Book of World Records. She crocheted a wearable bucket hat while blindfolded and singing in multiple languages. The school celebrated the feat as a demonstration of concentration, creativity and exceptional multitasking abilities.

stories.title: Karimnagar student qualifies for state-level archery
stories.summary: Vinmayi, a Grade VII student at St George International School, has qualified for state-level archery competitions. She secured a bronze medal in the Under-14 category at a district-level tournament held on November 22. The state-level event is scheduled to take place on November 28 in Nirmal.

stories.title: Three CFAL students qualify for Regional Mathematical Olympiad
stories.summary: Three students from the Centre for Advanced Learning in Mangaluru have qualified for the Regional Mathematical Olympiad. The students achieved their spots through the Indian Olympiad Qualifier in Mathematics. The institution continues a 17-year legacy of participation in national and international mathematics competitions.

stories.title: Bangladesh selects six students for science olympiad in Bulgaria
stories.summary: Six students will represent Bangladesh at the 23rd International Junior Science Olympiad in Sofia, Bulgaria, this December. The team was selected through the 12th Bangladesh Junior Science Olympiad. Participants from nearly 50 countries are expected to compete in the science event for students under 16.

stories.title: UIT teams rank in top 10 of AI Olympiad
stories.summary: Three teams from the University of Information Technology in Vietnam placed in the top 10 at the Southern Regional Round of the 2026 Student Artificial Intelligence Olympiad. The competition required teams to demonstrate algorithmic thinking and the ability to apply AI to solve practical problems.

stories.title: Taein Sports awards scholarships to Olympic and Asian Games winners
stories.summary: The 37th Taein Sports Scholarship Ceremony was held on November 26 at the Jincheon National Training Center. Gold medalists Choi Ga-on and Kang Joon were among the recipients. The scholarship project has awarded 867 grants over 37 years to foster athletic dreamers with the right personality.

stories.title: Infosys Prize awarded to researcher using Wi-Fi for robotics
stories.summary: Swarun Kumar, an IIT Madras alumnus at Carnegie Mellon University, has won the 2026 Infosys Prize. His research explores using radio waves to sense surroundings and power soft robots without batteries. The technology aims to take wireless signals beyond standard internet connectivity to locate objects and move hardware.

stories.title: Mumbai student develops battery-free groundwater sensor
stories.summary: Kaavya Majumder, a Class 11 student in Mumbai, has deployed a battery-free groundwater monitoring system called JalYantra in rural Maharashtra. The device tracks water levels and recovery without internet connectivity. The system is designed to assist communities that rely on wells but lack reliable monitoring infrastructure.

stories.title: Birla Open Minds hosts student innovation fair
stories.summary: Birla Open Minds International School in Pampore held its Kaushalbodh Mela 2026 on Wednesday. The event provided a platform for students to showcase practical skills, innovative ideas and creativity. The fair was inaugurated by local officials and educators to highlight student talent and project-based learning.

stories.title: US researchers develop AI tool to verify medical summaries
stories.summary: Health systems are increasingly using AI to summarize patient records, requiring clinicians to manually verify the output. A team from UW Health and Epic has now built a second AI system to review the first one's work. The machine is now checking the machine.

stories.title: Social robots improve Chinese character recognition in second grade
stories.summary: A study published in AI, Brain and Child found that integrating social robots into second-grade Chinese language lessons improved character recognition compared to standard instruction. The investigation tracked eighty-seven students over an eight-week cycle to measure literacy gains and engagement levels during teacher-led classroom activities.

stories.title: Australian student success rates surge as AI use grows
stories.summary: Australian university attrition rates have dropped to 10.7 percent, the lowest figure in two decades. While the Department of Education credits various initiatives, insiders suggest the turnaround may be linked to students outsourcing their coursework to bots. Success is now a matter of perspective.

stories.title: Schools lack national guidance on AI use in student reports
stories.summary: Federal law requires schools to provide understandable reports to parents, but there is no consistent national policy on using AI to generate them. In New South Wales, public school teachers are already using a state-provided platform to assist with comments. Clarity remains a work in progress.

stories.title: Agriculture students embrace AI but value traditional skills
stories.summary: Students at Bishop Burton and Riseholme colleges are learning to integrate AI into land-based studies while maintaining a focus on traditional methods. Despite the technological shift, pupils emphasize that AI cannot perform physical tasks like delivering a lamb. Some skills remain stubbornly analog.

stories.title: SAI International hosts 10th annual STEM conclave
stories.summary: The 10th SAITED STEM conclave in Bhubaneswar brought together over 4,482 students from 60 schools. The event featured a student startup accelerator and was attended by former ISRO Satellite Centre director Dr Mylswamy Annadurai. The theme for the decadal edition was engineering the impossible.

stories.title: Google launches free AI training for Australian teachers
stories.summary: Google has introduced a training program for Australian educators featuring lessons on Gemini for Education. The initiative includes a tool designed to convert dense history texts into illustrated worksheets. Modules take 15 to 30 minutes to complete, and participants can earn digital micro-credentials for their time.

stories.title: Turkmenistan hosts 5th International Chemistry Olympiad
stories.summary: Around 260 students from eight countries are competing in the 5th International Chemistry Olympiad at Magtymguly Turkmen State University. The event includes both individual and team events across two levels of difficulty. Participants represent 50 higher education institutions from across the region.

stories.title: CBSE releases 2027 Class 10 social science study material
stories.summary: The CBSE has published study materials for the 2027 Class 10 social science board exams. The guide covers history, geography, political science, and economics, emphasizing a strategic approach to mastering facts and competency-based questions. Students are encouraged to balance their preparation across all four books.

stories.title: Parents seek answers as children struggle with reading
stories.summary: Parents are increasingly concerned about early reading milestones as academic expectations rise. While some children require extra time to develop phonics and recognition skills, others find success through exposure to graphic novels. The search for the right reading pace continues to occupy family mornings.

stories.title: IIT Madras activates GATE 2027 mock tests
stories.summary: The Indian Institute of Technology Madras has released online mock tests for the GATE 2027 examination. Candidates can access paper-wise practice links on the official website to familiarize themselves with the computer-based interface. The tests are intended to help students prepare for the upcoming national entrance exam.

stories.title: IIT Madras updates GATE 2027 syllabus and mock tests
stories.summary: IIT Madras has activated mock test links for GATE 2027, which now includes a new test paper for Robotics and Automation. The examination authority has also revised the syllabus and exam pattern. Admit cards are expected to be released soon ahead of the February testing window.

stories.title: GATE 2027 Mock Test Link Activated at gate2027.iitm.ac.in: Know Pattern and Difficulty Level - Shiksha.com
Students rely on peer advice despite rising AI usage
stories.summary: While students are increasingly using AI tools to research study abroad opportunities, they continue to prioritize the opinions of current and former students. Peer influence remains a primary driver for validating information found on institutional websites and through automated AI platforms.

stories.title: UCAS website remains top destination for clearing research
stories.summary: Despite the widespread adoption of AI for schoolwork and research, UCAS reports that 56 percent of students used its website to prepare for Clearing in 2026. University websites followed at 43 percent. AI has yet to dampen the demand for official institutional information.

stories.title: Tashkent hosts Asian International Student Olympiad in Surgery
stories.summary: Twenty-two student teams from four Central Asian countries participated in the international surgery Olympiad in Tashkent. The four-day event evaluated theoretical knowledge and practical skills across 15 surgical branches. The competition aimed to facilitate experience exchange among young medical specialists.

stories.title: Vietnam launches 8th National English Olympiad
stories.summary: The Ho Chi Minh Communist Youth Union has launched the 8th National High School and University Student English Olympiad. The competition includes online preliminary rounds running through February 2027. The event is organized in collaboration with IIG Vietnam to assess student competency nationwide.

stories.title: South African students invited to apply for 2027 scholarship
stories.summary: The Babette Taute Trust is offering R50,000 in funding for South African students pursuing full-time Honours degrees in English language and literature. Applications are open for the 2027 academic year, providing financial assistance to those undertaking advanced studies in the field.

stories.title: Zhejiang University opens 2027 scholarship applications
stories.summary: Zhejiang University is accepting applications for master’s and PhD scholarships for the 2027 academic session. Funding schemes include the Chinese Government Scholarship and university-specific awards across disciplines ranging from engineering to humanities. Applications for the various programmes remain open through May 2027.

stories.title: King’s College London announces joint PhD scholarships
stories.summary: King’s College London is offering fully funded joint PhD scholarships for the 2027/28 academic year. The program covers tuition fees, a living stipend, and up to £5,000 in research funding. The initiative supports academic collaboration between the London institution and four global partner universities.

stories.title: Wageningen University offers 2027 master’s scholarships
stories.summary: Wageningen University and Research is promoting several scholarship programmes for prospective international master’s students for the 2027 to 2028 academic year. The institution notes that funding remains a primary factor for students considering an international education. The university is currently highlighting available options for incoming candidates.

stories.title: Oxford opens Mastercard Foundation scholarships for 2027
stories.summary: The University of Oxford is accepting applications for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program for the 2027/2028 academic year. In partnership with the Africa Oxford Initiative, the programme provides full funding for eligible one-year master’s degrees and postgraduate diplomas in global health research for African students.

stories.title: ETH Zurich invites applications for 2027 excellence scholarships
stories.summary: ETH Zurich has opened applications for its 2027 Excellence Scholarship and Opportunity Programme. The package includes a tuition waiver and CHF 13,500 per semester for master’s students. The deadline for submission is 30 November 2026. Academically exceptional students are encouraged to apply for the financial support.

stories.title: University of Bonn offers PhD workshop funding
stories.summary: The Right Livelihood College at the University of Bonn is offering fully funded scholarships for a December 2026 workshop on natural resource management. The event targets doctoral researchers from Africa, Asia, and Latin America currently studying in Germany. The workshop aims to connect experts with emerging scholars.

stories.title: Friends of Pakistan Fellowship opens for 2027
stories.summary: The Friends of Pakistan Fellowship is accepting applications for its 2027 cohort. The programme promises a seven-day retreat in Northern Pakistan where leaders refine their operating models to attract investors. The organisation claims to close the capital gap between global funders and scalable social businesses.

stories.title: Alum invests $50,000 in University of Arkansas scholarships
stories.summary: Mica Strother and Greg Hale have donated $50,000 to the Land of Opportunity Scholarship Endowment at the University of Arkansas. The funds are designated for students from Baxter and Sevier Counties with high financial needs. Strother is a graduate of Mountain Home High School.

stories.title: UP Board finalises 8,113 exam centres for 2027
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad has confirmed 8,113 examination centres for the 2027 Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations. The final list is now available on the board’s official website. Students can use the district-wise data to identify their assigned testing venues.

stories.title: HBSE 10th, 12th Exam Dates 2027 Announced, Detailed Datesheet Awaited - Shiksha.com
Haryana Board releases 2027 exam schedule
stories.summary: The Board of School Education Haryana has announced dates for the 2027 board examinations. Class 12 exams begin on March 3, while Class 10 exams start on March 4. The secondary examinations are scheduled to conclude on March 26, with senior secondary exams continuing until April 8.

stories.title: West Bengal HS Semester 3 results due tomorrow
stories.summary: The West Bengal Council of Higher Secondary Education will declare its Semester 3 results on November 27. Students can access their subject-wise marks and qualifying status online starting at 3 pm. The council plans to hold a press conference in Kolkata shortly before the digital release.

stories.title: UP Board publishes final 2027 exam centre list
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad has released the final list of 8,113 examination centres for the 2027 Class 10 and Class 12 exams. The document is available for download on the board’s website. School authorities and students can verify their assigned locations through the district-wise files.

stories.title: UPMSP confirms 8,113 exam centres for 2027
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad has finalised 8,113 examination centres for the 2027 board exams. The list received approval from the Examination Centre Determination Committee and is now accessible to the public. School authorities and parents may review the designated locations on the official website.

Foreign student visa numbers fall
International student numbers fall in UK
stories.summary: The number of non-EU overseas students arriving in the UK fell by 33,000 in the 12 months to June, according to ONS data. The government has been warned that the decline is damaging British universities and the wider economy. The trend continues despite the sector's reliance on international fees.

stories.title: Reform UK pledges to scrap graduate visa route
stories.summary: Reform UK has pledged to scrap graduate visas, describing the route as a scam used by low-skilled migrants to remain in Britain. The party claims 600,000 visas were issued in three years. Home Office statistics show 5,130 people held graduate visas in the year to June 2026.

stories.title: Mangaluru man arrested for alleged student visa fraud
stories.summary: Police in Porvorim arrested B P Manikanta for allegedly cheating a woman of 9.6 lakh rupees. The complainant stated she transferred the funds for a Canadian student visa, but the accused failed to provide the document or return the money. The suspect could not be traced initially.

stories.title: Graduate visa duration cut to 18 months
stories.summary: The UK government is reducing the duration of the Graduate visa from two years to 18 months for applications made on or after 1 January 2027. PhD graduates remain eligible for three years. The change applies based on the application date rather than the date of degree completion.

stories.title: Overseas student numbers decline by 33,000
stories.summary: The number of non-EU students arriving in the UK fell by 33,000 in the year to June, according to ONS figures. Home Office data indicates 335,801 study visas were granted in the year ending September 2026. The government has been warned this drop is damaging to universities.

stories.title: UK student visa rejection rate hits decade high
stories.summary: The UK student visa rejection rate reached 6.4 percent in the year ending September 2026, the highest level since 2015. The rate was 3.1 percent a year ago. Excluding Chinese applicants, the rejection rate rises to 8.2 percent. Visa application withdrawals have also increased during this period.

stories.title: UK Student Visa Rejection Rate Hits Decade High - Hamro Patro
Russell Group warns of student visa decline
stories.summary: Official statistics show a 12 percent drop in main international student applicants to the UK. The Russell Group warned the government that current policies are hitting demand. While 292,000 non-EU nationals left the UK, study-related arrivals fell by 11 percent compared to the previous year.

stories.title: Crucifer Academy expands into India
stories.summary: Crucifer Academy, a subsidiary of UAE-based Crucifer AI Technologies, has launched in India. The company aims to bridge the gap between education and employability by preparing learners for the technology sector. The academy is currently preparing for its first cohort under its Knowledge Guarantee program.

stories.title: LearningPad presents AI assessment tools
stories.summary: LearningPad showcased AI-powered assessment tools at the South India Educators’ Summit 2026. The company stated its approach supports teachers by identifying learning gaps while keeping human review as a safeguard. The presentation emphasized using technology to assist rather than replace professional judgement in the classroom.

stories.title: Ball State receives $12 million AI grant
stories.summary: Lilly Endowment Inc. awarded Ball State University a $12 million grant to fund a three-year AI training program starting in 2027. The university is among 35 Indiana institutions receiving a share of $292 million. The initiative aims to prepare students for careers in an AI-driven economy.

stories.title: Ball State gets $12M to bring AI training to students, faculty and staff - Cardinal Media
Nigeria launches National EdTech Strategy
stories.summary: The Nigerian government has introduced its first National Educational Technology Strategy. The initiative includes the AskFME AI Chatbot and a new education data portal. Developed with the Mastercard Foundation and World Bank, the strategy aims to integrate digital tools into classrooms and support teachers across the country.

stories.title: Teacher personalities in Kenyan schools
stories.summary: A study of Kenyan schools identifies 11 distinct teacher personalities. Despite sharing the same curriculum and staffroom, educators often exhibit different attitudes toward learners and institutional responsibilities. The teaching profession is described as a complex social environment where diverse workplace behaviours interact on a daily basis.

stories.title: Thousands of teachers await employment in Kenya
stories.summary: Kenya faces a teacher employment dilemma as 39,017 registered educators aged 45 and above remain outside the public payroll. Despite reported shortages in public schools, these qualified teachers have yet to secure positions with the Teachers Service Commission. The figures highlight ongoing recruitment challenges within the education sector.

stories.title: TSC proposes new teacher qualification rules
stories.summary: The Teachers Service Commission has proposed amendments to the Code of Regulations for Teachers to align with the Competency-Based Education system. The changes, discussed with a parliamentary committee, seek to update professional development and qualification standards. The commission is currently reviewing these regulations following public consultation.

stories.title: TSC considers stricter teacher certification rules
stories.summary: The Teachers Service Commission is reviewing regulations for teacher registration and professional certification. Proposed amendments to the Code of Regulations for Teachers have raised concerns regarding certificate renewal and potential removal from the payroll. The commission engaged with a parliamentary committee to discuss these updated professional standards.

stories.title: TSC reviews teacher registration regulations
stories.summary: The Teachers Service Commission has held discussions with a parliamentary committee regarding amendments to the Code of Regulations for Teachers. The proposed changes focus on Regulation 20, which governs academic and professional requirements for teacher registration. The commission is currently reviewing the framework following public consultation.

stories.title: MANUU hosts workshop for women teachers
stories.summary: The Centre for Women's Studies at Maulana Azad National Urdu University held a workshop for over 135 female teachers. The programme aimed to prepare participants for changing times by strengthening their teaching, research, financial and technological skills. The university intends to help teachers meet professional demands.

stories.title: Federal government to train 3,700 teachers
stories.summary: The National Teachers Institute and the Universal Basic Education Commission are launching a five-day training programme on Structured Pedagogy. The initiative aims to improve teaching methods across basic schools in two phases. The first phase will focus on 2,000 teachers across 19 northern states.

stories.title: The unseen pressures of public teaching in Kenya
stories.summary: Public school teachers face responsibilities beyond lesson planning and marking, including mentoring, counseling and navigating inadequate facilities. While society often measures success through examination results, the daily reality involves managing administrative demands and a changing education landscape. The profession remains defined by its hidden institutional pressures.

stories.title: Ghana Education Service opens teacher recruitment
stories.summary: The Ghana Education Service is seeking graduates with professional teaching qualifications for new vacancies. Applicants are expected to integrate 21st-century technology into their classrooms to improve learning outcomes. The service is looking for individuals who can address diverse educational needs through modern teaching methods.

stories.title: Indian government schools shift toward digital infrastructure
stories.summary: Indian government schools are moving away from overcrowded classrooms and traditional methods by adopting digital technology and upgraded facilities. The shift aims to make education more inclusive and effective. The focus is on preparing young minds through modernized learning environments rather than just renovating physical school buildings.

stories.title: Schools host workshop on gender-responsive teaching
stories.summary: The Sahodaya Faridabad Chapter and DAV Gian Prakash Chopra Public School held a professional development programme on gender-responsive approaches. The session aimed to sensitize educators on creating safe, inclusive and child-friendly environments. Several school principals participated in the capacity-building initiative for teachers.

stories.title: Lighthouse Learning partners with Kennedy High
stories.summary: Lighthouse Learning has announced a strategic partnership with Kennedy High The Global School in Hyderabad. The collaboration combines the school's two-decade legacy with the group's academic platform and national network. The partnership aims to support the school's next phase of growth and expand educational opportunities.

stories.title: 268 CBSE Schools Across 26 Countries, 21 Foreign Higher Education Institutions In India - شبكة تواصل الإخبارية
Education Ministry reports on global school presence
stories.summary: The Ministry of Education reports that 268 CBSE schools are now operational in 26 countries. During a consultative committee meeting, officials discussed strategies to internationalize Indian education and expand the global footprint of the Indian Knowledge System. Twenty-one foreign higher education institutions are currently active in India.

stories.title: Chowgule International School opens admissions
stories.summary: Chowgule International School in Goa has opened applications for the 2027-28 academic year. The school, part of the Chowgule Education Society, offers inquiry-led learning for grades ranging from Nursery to Grade 9. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking and applying academic concepts to real-world situations.

stories.title: Supreme Court clarifies CBSE language rules
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has intervened to address confusion regarding the CBSE three-language policy for the 2026-27 session. Students may retain their current two-language or three-language combinations for the remainder of the year. The court set these boundaries to prevent mid-year changes for students in classes 6 to 9.

stories.title: Supreme Court rules on CBSE language policy
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has clarified that CBSE students will not face mid-year language changes. Students currently studying two or three languages may continue their existing combinations for the 2026-27 session. The bench issued the order following a request from the CBSE to modify previous transitional relief.

stories.title: Court protects students from mid-year language shifts
stories.summary: A three-judge bench of the Supreme Court has ruled that CBSE students in classes 6 to 9 will not be required to change language combinations mid-year. Students may maintain their current two or three-language choices for the duration of the 2026-27 academic session.

stories.title: Education Ministry eyes global knowledge hub status
stories.summary: The Ministry of Education is planning to expand the international presence of Indian universities and attract more foreign students. Discussions at a recent parliamentary committee meeting focused on establishing foreign campuses in India and strengthening academic partnerships. The ministry aims to position India as a global knowledge hub.

stories.title: India presents 2036 Olympic vision
stories.summary: India has submitted its roadmap to the International Olympic Committee for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Ahmedabad serves as the central hub in the proposed hosting model. The selection process is expected to reach its next stage in March 2027.

stories.title: Government pushes for global higher education footprint
stories.summary: The Ministry of Education is taking steps to expand the global reach of the Indian Knowledge System. Officials confirmed that 21 foreign universities are now operational within India. The ministry is focusing on internationalizing the education system and establishing more academic partnerships with overseas institutions.

stories.title: MP High Court releases assistant grade 3 answer key
stories.summary: The High Court of Madhya Pradesh has published the model answer keys for its recent Assistant Grade 3 recruitment examination. Candidates can download the papers from the official website to verify their responses. The drive aims to fill 1,174 vacancies across district court establishments.

stories.title: High Court orders fresh UPPSC mains examination
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has quashed the 2025 Uttar Pradesh Assistant Prosecution Officer preliminary results. The court directed the commission to conduct the mains examination again after revising the preliminary list. The ruling emphasizes that meritorious reserved-category candidates must be considered for unreserved seats.

stories.title: NTA to release UGC NET city intimation slips
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency expects to release UGC NET December 2026 city intimation slips by November 25. The slip provides advance information on examination centre locations to help candidates plan travel. The agency notes the slip is not an admit card and does not contain final reporting details.

stories.title: UGC NET December 2026: NTA Provides Opportunity to Change Exam City - Shiksha.com
Kerala NEET PG round two allotment results released
stories.summary: The Commissioner of Entrance Examination has released the second phase final allotment results for Kerala NEET PG counselling 2026. The results cover government and private self-financing medical colleges across the state. Additional vacancies were identified following the publication of the initial list on November 26.

stories.title: NTA reopens exam city choice for thousands of candidates
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has reopened its exam city choice facility for 22,050 candidates who were originally assigned locations outside their four preferences. Affected students have until November 29 to select a new city. The exams are scheduled to take place from December 14.

stories.title: The intensity of the one-year master's degree
stories.summary: British universities have long offered one-year master's degrees, a model built on intensity and focus. The format assumes students have already identified their specific area of study. The programs are presented as an alternative philosophy of graduate education rather than an accelerated or watered-down version of American degrees.

stories.title: Germany remains a destination for tuition-free study
stories.summary: Germany continues to offer tuition-free higher education at public universities for undergraduate, master's and PhD students. While some programs do not require IELTS scores, there is no blanket rule for all international applicants. The country remains a primary destination for students seeking affordable European degrees.

stories.summary: The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa ranked 240th in Forbes’ 2027 America’s Top Colleges list. The ranking evaluated 1,600 institutions based on measurable outcomes like alumni earnings, student debt and graduation rates. It excluded institutional reputation as a primary metric in favor of return on investment.

stories.title: Queen Mary researchers cited among world's top 1%
stories.summary: Multiple Queen Mary University academics have been named among the world’s most highly cited researchers for 2026. The university credits the inclusion to its research excellence in fields including cancer, pharmacology and electronics. The institution maintains that this recognition confirms its status as a world-leading research center.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu Governor seeks intervention on university appointments
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has requested Chief Minister Vijay’s intervention to resolve the appointment of vice-chancellors. The Governor is pushing for a UGC nominee to be included in search committees, a move previously rejected by the state government. The two sides remain in a long-standing procedural dispute.

stories.title: Fee fixation committee vacancy stalls 1,700 applications
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu fee fixation committee has 1,700 pending applications due to the absence of a chairperson since June 30. Activists warn the vacancy could allow private schools to raise fees without oversight. The state government has missed its own deadline to appoint a replacement for the role.

stories.title: Trinity sustainability ranking faces internal criticism
stories.summary: A letter to the editor at Trinity College Dublin argues that the university's high sustainability ranking masks a lack of meaningful action. The author cites a 2025 climate roadmap which admits the university faces significant challenges in meeting its 2030 emission reduction targets despite its public sustainability messaging.

stories.title: Study visa grants fall to lowest levels since 2021
stories.summary: Home Office figures show 335,801 sponsored study visas were granted in the year to September 2026, a 23 percent decline. Main applicant numbers fell to 322,287, while dependant visas dropped by one third. International students remain the primary factor keeping net migration figures above zero.

research.title: Atunda: Building an Afrogenic Dance Movement Dataset for AI-Driven Classification
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper introduces Atunda, the first systematically collected video dataset of Afrogenic dance moves, designed for training and evaluating deep learning models for movement classification. The first phase of the dataset includes nearly 400 videos covering. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Decision and Support Mechanisms under Platform Information Overload: A Generative-Agent Experiment on College Application
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: People now make major personal decisions surrounded by far more online information than they can read, yet research says little about why information overload affects some people more than others. We study this question in Chinese. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Learning the Platform, Not the Learner: Sequencing Shortcuts in the Offline Evaluation of Educational Recommender Systems and LLM Rankers
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Educational recommenders are usually compared offline, by how well they predict the next activity in logs of tutoring systems, learning applications and MOOCs, where the next activity is largely decided by the platform: teachers assign problem. They bring AI models into scope and call. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Prompt Engineer: Analyzing Hard and Soft Skill Requirements in the AI Job Market
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has prompted speculation about a new job role: the prompt engineer. However, empirical evidence on how common such positions are and what skills employers expect of them remains scarce. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools now write, explain, and debug code, which changes how computing students learn and how their work is assessed. research.title: Towards Democratized Academic LLM Hosting: Practical insights from needs, implementations, and governance across Dutch institutions
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Academic LLM hosting is emerging as an operational infrastructure domain with recurring socio-technical patterns, tensions, and governance requirements across institutions. Based on a workshop with academic infrastructure, research-support, education, and policy-adjacent stakeholders, this paper synthesizes current. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
